## Investigation summary

I cold-launched `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` 8 times (force-stop → launch → Home → About → Diagnostics each time) and recorded the "Sync status" text and whether "Retry sync" appeared in the UI element tree:

| Run | Sync status text | "Retry sync" button |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 2 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 3 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 4 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 5 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 6 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 7 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 8 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |

5/8 present (62.5%) — matches the reported ~3-in-5 pass rate closely.

## What the button depends on

**It's tied 1:1 to the "Sync status" text, not to any layout/timing issue.** When status reads "Sync idle," the Retry sync view exists as a full clickable element in the tree. When status reads "Sync unavailable," the button isn't hidden or disabled — it's absent from the tree entirely (the whole clickable node + its text child are missing), meaning it's conditionally composed only in the "idle" branch.

Ruled out via targeted tests:
- **Not a stale-render/navigation-speed race** — I tried both immediate back-to-back taps and normally-paced navigation; outcome showed no correlation with speed.
- **Not something that resolves over time** — within a single process, going Diagnostics → Back → Diagnostics again repeatedly kept returning the *same* status every time (never flipped mid-session). The value is fixed once at process start, not recomputed on each screen visit.
- **Not build/channel-dependent** — "Build channel: BENCH-STABLE" was identical on every run.
- **Not a real network check** — the app's own About text states it "has no network access," so "sync" is a simulated/fake status, not backed by connectivity.

## Conclusion

The flake source is a **per-cold-start randomized sync-status value** baked into the Diagnostics screen: each fresh process launch appears to draw a fresh idle/unavailable state (roughly 60/40 in favor of "idle") independent of device state, timing, or navigation path. The "Retry sync" button is only composed when that draw lands on "idle," so any test asserting the button is unconditionally visible will fail whenever the app happens to boot into the "unavailable" branch — which explains the observed ~3-out-of-5 pass rate almost exactly.

I attempted to confirm this at the source level (the build is debuggable — `spectra_attach` succeeded), but without the app's class names I couldn't set a targeted breakpoint to catch the exact random draw. The black-box evidence above (fixed-per-process, no timing/network/build correlation, consistent ~60% split matching the reported flake rate) is strong enough to identify the mechanism, but I'd recommend the team point me at the Diagnostics ViewModel/composable source (or share the APK's `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` package structure) if they want the exact randomization call pinned down line-by-line.

**Recommendation for the test:** don't assert "Retry sync" is unconditionally visible — assert on `Sync status == "Sync idle" implies Retry sync visible` (or force a deterministic sync state before the assertion) instead.
